items.title: Vercel ships eve 1.0: an open-source framework for production agents, now GA
items.summary: GA after 230+ releases since the June preview. The harness handles model calls, tool runs and subagent delegation; the open-source Workflow SDK checkpoints progress so an agent resumes after a crash; multiplayer sessions, multi-tenant agents, cross-session memory, and OpenTelemetry tracing are built in. Rillet built a software-factory agent on eve (request to spec to test to PR) and tripled its shipping rate in three months. Clay's data agent "monty" is used weekly by 30-40% of the company just two months in.
items.why: This is a production-grade agent harness with real adoption numbers behind it, not another agent-framework announcement no one is actually running.
items.action: Skim the "software factory" pattern (request to spec to test to PR) against your own cross-service code generation ideas.

items.title: Google open-sources ABFS: cuts Android's 36-minute checkout to under 8 seconds
items.summary: A content-addressable virtual filesystem plus build cache that lazy-loads Git objects on demand and reuses build outputs across CI and local machines. On AOSP: checkout time dropped from about 36 minutes to under 8 seconds, full build time from about 80 minutes to just over 2 minutes, with up to 100% build-action reuse across CI and developer workspaces. Built so multiple agent orchestrators can run parallel workspaces without each paying the full sync-and-build cost. Now open source on GitHub.
items.why: If a build loop pays a multi-minute tax before every change, this is the actual plumbing fix, backed by hard before/after numbers rather than a benchmark claim.
items.action: Check the architecture against whatever monorepo tooling is already in use.

items.title: OpenAI's own data on AI research acceleration: agents finish 46% of 2-4hr tasks alone, but the gains are jagged
items.summary: Posted via @OpenAI linking a research report. Over several months, autonomous agent success rose 23%-46% on 2-4hr tasks and 13%-35% on 4-8hr tasks, but it is sharply task-dependent: 79% success monitoring training runs vs 35% launching them vs 25% writing inference/serving code. Median researcher agent spend hit $2,400/day, up 62% month over month; the 90th percentile hit $23,000/day, up 105%. Asked what they would trade to keep frontier coding agents for three months, researchers' median answers were 30% of team compute, or separately, 40% of team headcount.
items.why: A company publishing its own jagged, task-by-task agent success rates, not one clean benchmark number, is a rare concrete look at where agent autonomy still breaks down.
items.action: The task-type breakdown is a template for auditing which of your own agent workflows are actually reliable versus which just look good in a demo.

items.title: LangSmith now ties coding-agent spend directly to merged PRs — across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot
items.summary: A new "coding agent" type in LangSmith's Agent Platform attributes every trace's spend to the pull requests it produced, splits cost by PR state (open, closed, merged) and by work type (features, bug fixes, investigation/review), and tracks "unattributed" spend — review work that never produced a PR — separately. Built after the vendor's own coding-agent spend, on an internal agent, started climbing. Context: coding is now the largest category of enterprise AI spend, $34B in 2026.
items.why: This turns "our coding agent costs X" into "here's what X is actually buying" — the exact question anyone with a coding-agent budget gets asked and usually can't answer.
items.action: The open/closed/merged-PR cost split is worth stealing even without this specific tool, for tracking coding-agent spend anywhere.
